record.original_question: Determine whether quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be desingularized in every complex dimension n >= 3 in the same sense known in dimensions at most 2, namely after suitable blow-ups separating divisorial singularities from a residual positive current with arbitrarily small Lelong numbers.

evidence.quote: Question 34 (Favre-Guedj-Jonsson). Can one similarly desingularize quasi-plurisubharmonic functions in any dimension n >= 3 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$ and let $\varphi$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on $X$ (i.e., $\varphi$ is locally the sum of a smooth function and a plurisubharmonic function, equivalently $dd^c \varphi \geq -\omega$ for some smooth $(1,1)$-form $\omega$). In complex dimension at most 2, it is known that $\varphi$ can be desingularized as follows: there exists a finite composition of blow-ups $\pi : \tilde{X} \to X$ with smooth centers such that the pull-back $\pi^* \varphi$ decomposes as 
$$\pi^* \varphi = \sum_{j} a_j \log |f_j| + \psi,$$
where $\sum_j a_j \log |f_j|$ is a divisorial part with $f_j$ local equations of exceptional or strict transform divisors and $a_j \geq 0$, and $\psi$ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function whose associated positive $(1,1)$-current $dd^c \psi + \pi^*\omega$ has arbitrarily small Lelong numbers everywhere on $\tilde{X}$.

Question: Does an analogous desingularization statement hold for every quasi-plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold of arbitrary dimension $n \geq 3$?
artifact.status_search_result: A two-dimensional desingularization result for quasi-plurisubharmonic functions is established via the valuative analysis of Favre–Jonsson and related work (Guedj, "Desingularization of quasiplurisubharmonic functions," 2005). Extensions of valuative methods to higher dimensions (Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson) have been developed, but a direct search did not surface a definitive solution to the higher-dimensional ($n \geq 3$) desingularization question in the same form. Status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Valuative analysis of planar plurisubharmonic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Valuative analysis of singularities of psh functions established in dimension 2.
status_evidence.claim: The two-dimensional case is established by Favre–Jonsson via valuative analysis.

status_evidence.title: Valuations and Plurisubharmonic Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Extends valuative techniques to higher dimensions, describing valuation spaces on C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional valuative framework exists but a direct desingularization analogue is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Continuous approximation of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions
status_evidence.claim: Related approximation/regularization results exist but do not constitute the requested desingularization.
